cards.explanation: The prophet is Ahijah, friends, and Jeroboam names him himself in verse 2. Back in 1 Kings 11:29-31, Ahijah the Shilonite met Jeroboam on the road and tore a new cloak into twelve pieces. Now Jeroboam is sending his wife to that same prophet.

The answer is boy, friends. Jeroboam says it plainly in verse 3: "He will tell you what will become of the boy." His son Abijah is sick, and that's the whole reason for the trip. I think that tells you where Jeroboam's heart is right now.

The answer is the LORD, friends. Verse 5 says He let Ahijah know that Jeroboam's wife was coming about her sick son, and that she would be disguised. Ahijah can't see a thing, but he got the full report from the One who can. So that disguise was walking into a plan it never knew about.

The answer is False, friends. In verse 5 the LORD tells Ahijah, "You are to say such and such to her…" so he has a message ready. She won't leave without an answer. I think it's an answer she won't want, though.

The answer is True, and Ahijah doesn't waste a second. He hears her at the door and says, "Come in, wife of Jeroboam! Why are you disguised?" (1 Kings 14:6). Somebody at the costume shop is getting a strongly worded review.

The answer is bad news, friends. Ahijah says it in his own words: "…I have been sent to you with bad news." (1 Kings 14:6). She came hoping for an answer about her boy, and he doesn't dress it up. I think that's a heavy thing to hear at a door.

The answer is that David followed God with all his heart. Here God is speaking, and in verse 8 He says David "…kept My commandments and followed Me with all his heart, doing only what was right in My eyes." That's the measure God holds up. It's about David's heart following Him. Heart first, friends, always.

The answer is True, friends, and God doesn't soften it: "You have done more evil than all who came before you." (1 Kings 14:9). That's a heavy sentence. It comes right after God reminds Jeroboam in verses 7 and 8 of what he was given.

The answer is other gods and metal idols, friends. Verse 9 says, "You have proceeded to make for yourself other gods and molten images…" Molten images are idols made of metal. God says it was to provoke Him. Hands made them, and that's the problem.

The answer is that God will cut off every male in the house of Jeroboam. He says, "I will cut off from Jeroboam every male, both slave and free, in Israel…" (1 Kings 14:10). That's a heavy line, friends, and I'll just say it plainly. I think this one hurts.

The answer is when her feet enter the city, friends. Ahijah says it in verse 12: "When your feet enter the city, the child will die." I think this is the hardest line in the whole passage. It's a heavy part, so I'll let his words stand.

The answer is False, friends. Ahijah says, "All Israel will mourn for him and bury him." (1 Kings 14:13). Verse 18 says they buried him and all Israel mourned. That's a whole nation grieving, and it's a heavy moment.

The answer is that the LORD found some good in him, friends. Ahijah gives the reason in verse 13: "…only in him has the LORD, the God of Israel, found any good in the house of Jeroboam." Out of a whole house, one boy is singled out. I think that's a quiet kindness tucked inside a hard message.

The answer is True, friends. Verse 14 says the LORD "…will raise up for Himself a king over Israel who will cut off the house of Jeroboam." The king is raised up for the LORD Himself. That matches verse 10, where the house of Jeroboam was already named in the disaster.

The answer is a reed shaken in the water, friends. Ahijah says the LORD will strike Israel "…as a reed is shaken in the water." (1 Kings 14:15). I think the picture is of something that can't hold steady when the water moves it. That's a shaky place to stand.

The answer is fathers, friends. Verse 15 says the LORD will uproot Israel "…from this good land that He gave their fathers…" It was a gift to those who came before them. To be uprooted from a gift is a heavy thing.

The answer is Jeroboam's, friends. Verse 16 says God will give Israel over "…on account of the sins Jeroboam has committed and has caused Israel to commit." That's two things: what he did and what he led others into. Leaders carry a lot, friends.

The answer is True, friends. Verse 17 says, "…as soon as she stepped over the threshold of the house, the boy died." Ahijah had told her it would happen when her feet entered the city (1 Kings 14:12). It's a heavy moment, and I'll keep it quiet.
The answer is Nadab, friends. Verse 20 says, "…his son Nadab reigned in his place." Jeroboam ruled twenty-two years, and then the throne goes to Nadab. Passed along like a recipe card, friends.
